facts: The appellant worked as a daily wager under the respondent from 01.06.1988.
His services were dispensed with in December, 1993.

He served a notice of demand dated 30.12.1997 on the respondent contending that his services were terminated orally without complying with the mandatory provisions of Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and that he may be re-instated in service with full back wages from the date of illegal termination and he may be regularized according to Government policy.
The respondent did not respond to the demand made by the appellant and by order dated 23.07.1999, the State Government referred the dispute under Section 10 of the Act to the Labour Court.
The appellant and the respondent filed their claim-statement and the objection respectively before the Labour Court, Rohtak, and led evidence in support of their respective cases.
issues: Whether the High Court was right in setting aside the Award dated 18.07.2006 of the Labour Court directing reinstatement of the appellant with 50% back wages and directing instead payment of compensation of Rs.50,000/- to the appellant.
petitioner_arguments: The Labour Court having found that these pre-conditions had not been complied with in the case had rightly directed re-instatement of the appellant with 50% back wages.
This is not a fit case where the appellant could be regularized in service.
respondent_arguments: The High Court has relied on the decisions of this Court in Mahboob Deepak v. Nagar Panchayat, Gajraula & Anr. and Ghaziabad Development Authority & Anr. v. Ashok Kumar & Anr.
This is not a fit case where the appellant could be regularized in service.
court_reasoning: The Labour Court has exercised its jurisdiction in the facts and circumstances of the case to direct re-instatement of a workman with 50% back wages taking into consideration the pleadings of the parties and the evidence on record.
Wide discretion is, therefore, vested in the Labour Court while adjudicating an industrial dispute relating to discharge or dismissal of a workman.
holding: The High Court was wrong in setting aside the Award dated 18.07.2006 of the Labour Court directing reinstatement of the appellant with 50% back wages and instead payment of compensation of Rs.50,000/- to the appellant.
